renderings.value: Expresses an action that occurs immediately after another action; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than', 'the moment'.

The ～か～ないかのうちに grammar point is used to express that an action occurs immediately after another action. In English, it can be translated as 'as soon as', 'no sooner than', or 'the moment'. This grammar point is used with verbs, showing the verb in both affirmative and negative forms with か and ないか, followed by のうちに.
Verb-casual + か + Verb-negative form + かのうちに
Neutral "just as/almost before" - emphasizes the two actions nearly overlapping.
No sooner had I arrived at the station than it started raining.
As soon as I decided to buy the cell phone, a new model was released.
The moment he left the house, the phone rang.
As soon as the party began, she started crying.
